songs.title: First Thing You See
songs.treatment: Moonlit UK garage pop, about 126 BPM. The flower's rule (love the first live thing you see) is the chorus and the camera's logic.
songs.narrative_lens: An unseen forest voice telling the story in present tense with crisp rhymed couplets. Each time someone wakes, the plot turns.
songs.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Four more days till the wedding bells,
Theseus and Hippolyta, Athens swells.
Egeus drags Hermia up to the throne:
wed Demetrius, the man I chose.
She loves Lysander. The duke is clear:
obey, or die, or a nun's cold years.
So they'll slip through the wood tomorrow night
to his aunt's, out of the law's sight.

[Verse 2]
Helena loves Demetrius; he loves her friend.
She tells him they're running, hoping he'll bend.
He races for the wood, she races behind.
And Quince's craftsmen have a play in mind:
Bottom the weaver will be Pyramus,
Thisbe's lover, for the wedding feast,
rehearsing by moonlight where nobody sees.

[Chorus]
Close your eyes, then open: the first thing you see,
that's who you'll love, that's who you'll be.
Moonlight, moonlight, nobody's free,
first thing you see, first thing you see.

[Verse 3]
Deep in the trees there's a fairy war,
Oberon and Titania fighting for
a boy she raises for his mother's sake,
her friend who died. Now the seasons break,
the rivers flood. Oberon wants the boy;
he sends Puck for a flower he knows:
drip it on sleeping eyes, and the sleeper goes
wild for the first live creature it sees.

[Verse 4]
He hears Demetrius drive Helena away:
Puck, charm that Athenian, turn his heart her way.
He drips the juice on his sleeping queen.
Puck spots Athenian clothes on a man in a dream.
Wrong man. Lysander wakes to Helena's face,
swears he loves her, leaves Hermia in that place.
Helena thinks it's a cruel joke and flees;
Hermia wakes up alone in the trees.

[Chorus]
Close your eyes, then open: the first thing you see,
that's who you'll love, that's who you'll be.
Moonlight, moonlight, nobody's free,
first thing you see, first thing you see.

[Verse 5]
Puck sets a donkey's head on Bottom's own;
the craftsmen scatter, he sings alone.
Titania wakes, charmed, loves the weaver on sight,
sends fairies to serve him all through the night.
Oberon sees the slip and charms Demetrius himself.
Now both men chase Helena: you're mocking me, she yells.
Hermia's furious, betrayed and confused,
and the rivals stalk off to find a place to duel.

[Bridge]
Puck brings the fog, borrows each man's voice,
leads them in circles till they've got no choice:
four asleep on the dew-wet ground.
The cure goes on Lysander's eyes alone.
Demetrius still wears the spell.

[Verse 6]
Oberon says the charmed queen gave up the boy.
He frees her eyes. Puck lifts the donkey head away,
Bottom's own face underneath. The fairies make peace.
Dawn horns: Theseus finds the four asleep,
overrules Egeus: you'll marry when I do.
Lysander's cured, and back with Hermia;
Demetrius, still enchanted, loves Helena.
Bottom wakes with a dream he can't explain
and runs to his crew, who cheer his name.

[Verse 7]
Married now, three couples watch the play:
a Wall, a Lion whose bloody mouth stains Thisbe's cloak.
Pyramus finds it, thinks she's dead, and stabs himself;
she finds him and does the same. Only actors.
The court heckles; Bottom sits up to offer a dance,
and midnight sends them all to bed.

[Final Chorus]
Close your eyes, then open: the first thing you see,
that's who you'll love, that's who you'll be.
Moonlight, moonlight, nobody's free,
first thing you see, first thing you see.

[Outro]
Fairies bless the house, Puck sweeps the door.
Puck says, if we offended, call it a dream;
pardon us, and we'll mend.
Give us your hands.
songs.style_prompt: UK garage pop, about 126 BPM. Swung two-step drums with crisp shuffled hi-hats, a deep rounded sub bass, plucked bell-like keys and soft pad chords. Clear, bright female lead sung close and fairly dry in the verses so names and plot turns stay intelligible; light doubling only on line endings. Verses stay lean: drums, bass and one key line. Chorus opens wide with stacked harmonies, a brighter chord lift and a sub drop on the downbeat. Bridge thins to a filtered beat, keys and voice, then a short two-bar instrumental gap. Final chorus adds an extra harmony layer and a short synth answer phrase. Clean, close, uncluttered mix with the vocal forward.
songs.exclude_styles: heavy autotune, rap verses, distorted vocals, washed-out reverb, EDM festival build-ups, comedic voices

songs.title: Mine Own and Not Mine Own
songs.treatment: Intimate art pop and indietronica, about 86 BPM. Helena's line about finding Demetrius 'like a jewel, mine own and not mine own' becomes an open question.
songs.narrative_lens: The narrator speaks to Helena as 'you' through the whole story. The chorus is in Helena's own voice.
songs.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
You loved him first, Helena,
before he turned his oaths toward Hermia.
Now Theseus counts four days to wed Hippolyta,
and Egeus tells the court his daughter must obey:
marry Demetrius, or the law decides,
death, or a nun's life under a barren moon.
She loves Lysander. Tomorrow night
they'll slip through the wood to his aunt's, past the rule.

[Verse 2]
They trust you with the secret as they go.
You carry it to Demetrius, hoping he'll be grateful;
he runs into the wood for Hermia, and you run after him.
That same night Quince's workmen gather in the trees
to rehearse a play for the wedding:
Bottom the weaver as Pyramus,
kept from his Thisbe by a wall.

[Chorus]
Mine own, and not mine own,
a jewel I found but never earned.
Mine own, and not mine own,
who lit the lamp in him when he turned?

[Verse 3]
In that wood a fairy king and queen are at war
over a boy whose mother, Titania's friend, has died;
she keeps him for her sake. Their quarrel floods the fields
and puts frost on summer roses. Oberon wants the boy.
He sends Puck for a flower: a drop on sleeping eyes,
and the waker loves the first live thing it sees.

[Verse 4]
He watches Demetrius threaten you and go,
and softens: Puck, charm that Athenian for her.
He paints his sleeping queen. Puck finds Athenian clothes:
Lysander, not Demetrius. The wrong eyes.
You wake him; he swears he loves you, leaves her sleeping.
You think it's cruel mockery, and run.
Hermia wakes from a serpent dream, alone.

[Chorus]
Mine own, and not mine own,
a jewel I found but never earned.
Mine own, and not mine own,
who lit the lamp in him when he turned?

[Verse 5]
Puck gives Bottom a donkey's head; his friends flee.
Titania wakes, enchanted, and adores him; fairies wait on him.
Oberon sees the mistake and touches Demetrius' eyes himself.
Now both men swear love to you. You're sure it's a game,
and Hermia's in on it; she thinks you stole her love.
The men walk off to duel.

[Bridge]
Puck pulls down the fog and borrows their voices,
leads them apart till all four fall asleep.
He cures Lysander's eyes. Only his.
Demetrius still wears the flower.

[Verse 6]
Oberon says the charmed queen gave him the boy.
He frees her eyes; Puck lifts the donkey head from Bottom's own,
and the fairy rulers make their peace.
Horns: Theseus finds you sleeping and overrules Egeus;
three couples will marry, his among them.
Lysander loves Hermia again. Demetrius, still enchanted,
says some power brought him back to you, Helena.
Bottom wakes, can't tell his dream, and finds his friends.

[Verse 7]
Married now, you watch the workmen's play:
lovers whisper through a Wall; a Lion stains Thisbe's dropped cloak;
Pyramus thinks she's dead and stabs himself;
she finds him and does the same. Only acting.
Bottom sits up; the court laughs; the players dance.

[Final Chorus]
Mine own, and not mine own,
a jewel I found but never earned.
Mine own, and not mine own,
who lit the lamp in him when he turned?

[Outro]
Fairies bless the beds while the house sleeps.
Puck asks: if we offended, think it a dream,
and give us your hands.
Mine own, and not mine own.

songs.title: Never Ran Smooth
songs.treatment: Cinematic electronic metal, about 94 BPM. Lysander's 'the course of true love never did run smooth' becomes a defiant chorus. The heaviest dynamics are saved for the quarrel and the fog.
songs.narrative_lens: Terse, scene-stamped fragments ('Athens.', 'The wood.', 'Dawn.') with a Hermia-leaning tone. The chorus 'we' is a collective voice for the lovers.
songs.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Athens. A wedding in four days,
Theseus and Hippolyta.
Egeus drags his daughter in:
Hermia, take Demetrius.
She won't. She loves Lysander.
So the duke reads out the law:
die, or wear a nun's veil all your life.
Then the lovers plan to run
through the wood to his aunt's,
where Athens' law can't follow.

[Verse 2]
Helena loves Demetrius;
he wants Hermia instead.
She tells him of the flight
for one kind word.
He hunts the lovers;
she hunts him.
And Quince calls out his workmen:
Bottom gets Pyramus.
They'll rehearse their tragedy
for the duke's wedding night
deep in the same dark wood.

[Chorus]
Never ran smooth, never ran smooth,
true love was never going to run smooth.
Through the wood, through the fog, through the night,
it never ran smooth, but we ran.

[Verse 3]
The wood. A war of fairies.
Oberon wants a boy
Titania raises for his mother,
her friend who died.
She won't let him go.
Their quarrel drowns the fields,
frost lands on summer roses.
Oberon sends Puck for a flower:
drip it on sleeping eyes,
they'll love the first live thing they see.

[Verse 4]
He hears Demetrius drive Helena off:
Puck, charm that Athenian.
He streaks his sleeping queen himself.
Puck finds Athenian clothes,
Lysander, not Demetrius.
Wrong eyes. Helena wakes him;
he swears he loves her now
and leaves Hermia asleep.
Helena calls it mockery and flees.
Hermia wakes to an empty wood.

[Chorus]
Never ran smooth, never ran smooth,
true love was never going to run smooth.
Through the wood, through the fog, through the night,
it never ran smooth, but we ran.

[Verse 5]
Puck plants a donkey's head on Bottom.
His friends scream and scatter.
Titania wakes, enchanted,
and loves him; fairies serve him.
Oberon sees the error,
charms Demetrius himself.
Two men vowing love to Helena;
she's sure it's a cruel joke.
Hermia, robbed and called a puppet,
turns on her oldest friend.
The rivals leave to fight.

[Bridge]
Fog. Black fog.
Puck throws each rival's voice,
leads them apart in circles
till they drop. Four asleep.
Cure on Lysander's eyes.
Only his.
Demetrius stays enchanted.

[Verse 6]
Oberon says the charmed queen gave up the boy.
He frees her eyes.
Puck lifts the donkey head;
Bottom's own face returns.
The fairies make their peace.
Dawn. Horns. Theseus finds four asleep,
overrules Egeus: three weddings, his and theirs.
Lysander, cured, is Hermia's again.
Demetrius, still under the flower,
loves Helena.
Bottom wakes, can't say his dream,
runs back to his crew.

[Verse 7]
Night. Three couples, wed, watch the play.
A talking Wall. A Lion stains Thisbe's cloak;
Pyramus thinks she's dead,
stabs himself; she does the same.
Only actors falling.
Bottom sits up. The court laughs.
Two players dance; then midnight.

[Final Chorus]
Never ran smooth, never ran smooth,
true love was never going to run smooth.
Through the wood, through the fog, through the night,
it never ran smooth, but we ran.

[Outro]
Fairies bless the house.
Puck says, if we offended,
call it a dream, and pardon us.
Give us your hands.
It never ran smooth, but we ran.

songs.title: Lord, What Fools
songs.treatment: Alternative hip hop with a pop trap frame, about 96 BPM. Puck raps the whole story in first person. The sung refrain is built on his own line about mortals.
songs.narrative_lens: Puck as an amused, articulate narrator. Narrating the Athens scenes he never witnessed is storyteller license.
songs.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Listen. Four days till Theseus weds Hippolyta,
then Egeus storms the court with his daughter, Hermia:
she weds Demetrius, his pick, or she meets the law,
death, or a nun's cell, cold moon and all.
She loves Lysander, so the pair make a plan:
tomorrow night, through my wood, hand in hand,
to his aunt's house, out where Athens can't reach.

[Verse 2]
Helena loves Demetrius; he swore to her once,
then switched to Hermia. So she spills what she knows,
hoping for thanks. He chases them; she chases him.
Meanwhile Quince rounds up his working men,
Bottom the weaver cast as Pyramus,
rehearsing Pyramus and Thisbe for the wedding,
in my wood by moonlight. Bless 'em.

[Chorus]
Lord, what fools these mortals be,
running through the moonlight after what they can't see.
Lord, what fools, what fools these mortals be,
and the biggest fool's the one who swears he's free.

[Verse 3]
My king and queen? At war. She keeps a boy,
her dead friend's son, and she won't hand him over.
Their fight floods fields, puts frost on the roses.
So he sends me flying for a flower:
juice on sleeping eyes, you'll dote
on the first live thing you notice.
He hears Demetrius tell Helena to get lost:
Puck, charm that Athenian. Done. I'm gone.

[Verse 4]
He streaks the queen's eyes while she sleeps in her bower.
Me? I find Athenian clothes on a sleeping man,
a girl lying further off. Job done. Wrong man.
That was Lysander. Helena shakes him awake;
he swears he loves her, leaves Hermia cold.
Helena thinks he's mocking her and runs;
Hermia wakes alone, screaming his name.

[Chorus]
Lord, what fools these mortals be,
running through the moonlight after what they can't see.
Lord, what fools, what fools these mortals be,
and the biggest fool's the one who swears he's free.

[Verse 5]
Then I catch the players rehearsing near her bed,
give Bottom a donkey's head, just the head,
and his crew flies like geese at a gunshot.
Titania wakes, charmed, loves him, has her fairies wait on him.
My king sees my slip and charms Demetrius himself.
Now two men chase Helena; she says it's a cruel joke.
Hermia thinks she's been robbed. The boys go off to duel.

[Bridge]
So I roll in the fog, throw each rival's voice,
lead 'em up and down till they drop.
Four on the ground. Cure on Lysander's eyes,
only his. Demetrius stays charmed. Not my call.

[Verse 6]
My king says the queen, still charmed, gave up the boy.
He frees her eyes; I pull the donkey head off,
Bottom's own face safe underneath. King and queen dance.
Horns. Theseus finds the four, overrules Egeus.
Lysander's cured and back with Hermia;
Demetrius, still charmed, loves Helena;
three couples wed, the duke's among them.
Bottom wakes, can't explain his dream, runs to his crew.

[Verse 7]
Feast night, three couples watch the play:
a Wall with a chink, a Lion stains Thisbe's cloak,
Pyramus thinks she's dead and stabs himself;
she finds him, does the same. Fake blades.
Bottom pops back up; the court cracks jokes; two players dance.

[Final Chorus]
Lord, what fools these mortals be,
running through the moonlight after what they can't see.
Lord, what fools, what fools these mortals be,
and the biggest fool's the one who swears he's free.

[Outro]
Then we fairies bless the house and every bed.
If we shadows have offended, call it a dream;
pardon us, and give me your hands,
and Robin makes amends. Lord, what fools.

songs.title: Before the First Cock Crow
songs.treatment: Woodland future garage, about 122 BPM. Oberon's deadline (meet him 'ere the first cock crow', with the lark heard at dawn) becomes a countdown through the night.
songs.narrative_lens: A soft, nocturnal narrator who opens each verse with a time stamp (Daylight, Midnight, Later, Small hours, Grey light, Wedding night).
songs.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Daylight in Athens. Theseus counts four days
till he weds Hippolyta. Then Egeus makes his case:
Hermia must wed Demetrius,
or die, or live her whole life as a nun.
She loves Lysander. Whispering, they choose:
meet in the wood tomorrow night,
then on to his aunt's, beyond the law.

[Verse 2]
Helena loves Demetrius, who left her for Hermia.
She tells him the plan, hoping he'll be grateful.
Nightfall: he hunts the lovers; she hunts him.
Out the same gate, Quince leads his craftsmen
to rehearse a play for the wedding feast,
Pyramus and Thisbe, Bottom the weaver as Pyramus.

[Chorus]
Before the first cock crow, before the lark,
set it right, set it right in the dark.
Every heart's a wager, every eye's a mark,
before the first cock crow, before the lark.

[Verse 3]
Midnight. The fairy king and queen collide
over a boy she raises for her dead friend's sake.
Their quarrel swells the rivers, scrambles the seasons.
Oberon wants the boy. He sends Puck for a flower:
one drop on sleeping lids, and the sleeper wakes
in love with the first live creature in sight.
He hears Demetrius spurn Helena: charm that man.

[Verse 4]
Later. Oberon streaks his sleeping queen.
Puck finds a man asleep in Athenian clothes,
Lysander, not Demetrius, and charms the wrong eyes.
Helena shakes him; he wakes, swears he loves her,
leaves Hermia lying on the ground.
Helena thinks he mocks her, and runs;
Hermia wakes, calls his name, hears nothing.

[Chorus]
Before the first cock crow, before the lark,
set it right, set it right in the dark.
Every heart's a wager, every eye's a mark,
before the first cock crow, before the lark.

[Verse 5]
Small hours. Puck crowns Bottom with a donkey's head;
the craftsmen flee. Titania wakes, enchanted,
loves him, and sets her fairies to serve him.
Oberon finds the error and charms Demetrius himself.
Two men court Helena now; she calls it mockery.
Hermia feels betrayed. The rivals head off to duel.

[Bridge]
Puck drops the fog, speaks in each man's voice,
leads them apart until they fall.
Four asleep. He cures Lysander's eyes, only his;
Demetrius still wears the flower.

[Verse 6]
Grey light. Oberon says the charmed queen gave up the boy.
He frees her; Puck lifts the donkey head from Bottom's own.
King and queen dance, at peace. Then dawn horns:
Theseus finds the four and overrules Egeus;
three couples will wed, his own among them.
Lysander, cured, is Hermia's again;
Demetrius, still enchanted, loves Helena.
Bottom wakes past words and runs back to his crew.

[Verse 7]
Wedding night. Three couples watch the play:
a Wall, a Moon; the Lion stains Thisbe's cloak;
Pyramus thinks she's dead, stabs himself;
she finds him, does the same. Just actors.
The court jokes, Bottom springs up for a dance,
and midnight sends the lovers to their beds.

[Final Chorus]
Before the first cock crow, before the lark,
set it right, set it right in the dark.
Every heart's a wager, every eye's a mark,
before the first cock crow, before the lark.

[Outro]
Fairies bless the house before the day.
Puck says, if we offended, think you slept;
pardon us, and give us your hands.
Before the lark.

songs.title: Bottom's Dream (It Has No Bottom)
songs.treatment: Warm acoustic campfire pop, about 96 BPM. The singalong refrain modernizes Bottom's verdict on his dream.
songs.narrative_lens: A storyteller singing past-tense ballad quatrains, as if passing the story around a fire.
songs.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Theseus would wed Hippolyta
in four days' time, they say,
when Egeus brought his daughter in
and swore she must obey:
wed Demetrius, or the law
would claim her life instead,
or a nun's cold cell. She loved Lysander,
so they planned to steal away
through the wood to his aunt's house,
beyond the law's long sway.

[Verse 2]
Now Helena loved Demetrius,
who'd sworn to her, then strayed.
She told him of the runaways,
just hoping he'd be kind;
he went chasing after Hermia,
and she ran close behind.
And Quince's crew went out to practice
by moonlight, out of sight,
a play of Pyramus and Thisbe,
Bottom in the lead, for the wedding night.

[Chorus]
It's Bottom's dream, it has no bottom,
nothing's the way it seemed.
The eye can't hear, the ear can't see,
it has no bottom, Bottom's dream.

[Verse 3]
Out in that wood the fairy king
and queen were bitter foes
over a boy whose mother died,
her friend, so the story goes.
Their quarrel flooded every field
and turned the seasons wrong.
Oberon wanted the boy, and sent
for a flower, small and strong:
a drop on sleeping eyelids
makes you love the first live thing you see.

[Verse 4]
He saw Demetrius scorn Helena
and told Puck, charm that man.
He charmed his queen; but Puck found Lysander
in Athenian clothes, and ran
the juice on the wrong man's eyes.
Lysander woke to Helena,
swore love, and left Hermia there.
Helena thought he mocked her;
Hermia woke to empty air.

[Chorus]
It's Bottom's dream, it has no bottom,
nothing's the way it seemed.
The eye can't hear, the ear can't see,
it has no bottom, Bottom's dream.

[Verse 5]
Then Puck gave Bottom a donkey's head,
and all his friends took flight;
Titania woke, enchanted,
and loved him at first sight,
had her fairies scratch his ears
and bring him honey sweet.
Oberon saw Puck's mistake
and charmed Demetrius in his sleep.

[Verse 6]
Now two men begged for Helena;
she thought it all a game.
Hermia felt robbed and cheated,
and the rivals' tempers flamed.
They went to duel, but Puck brought fog,
spoke in each rival's name,
and led them round till all four slept
before the morning came.

[Bridge]
He cured Lysander's eyes, only his;
Demetrius kept the spell.
Oberon told how the charmed queen gave up the boy;
he freed her eyes as well.
Puck lifted the donkey head away
from Bottom's own, and the fairies danced.

[Verse 7]
At dawn the horns of Theseus
woke the lovers where they lay;
he overruled old Egeus:
three couples would wed that day.
Lysander, cured, was Hermia's;
Demetrius, still charmed, loved Helena.
Bottom woke with a dream he couldn't tell,
and ran back to his friends.

[Verse 8]
That night they played for three wed pairs:
through a Wall the lovers sighed,
a Lion stained Thisbe's cloak,
Pyramus thought she'd died
and stabbed himself; she found him, did the same,
all acting, while the court joked;
then Bottom sat up and offered a dance.

[Final Chorus]
It's Bottom's dream, it has no bottom,
nothing's the way it seemed.
The eye can't hear, the ear can't see,
it has no bottom, Bottom's dream.

[Outro]
Fairies blessed the beds; Puck swept the floor:
if we shadows have offended,
call it a dream, and pardon us.
Give us your hands. It has no bottom.

songs.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
I grow in a western field, far from the court
where Theseus counts four days to wed Hippolyta.
Egeus wants his Hermia to marry Demetrius,
or the law will take her life, or close her in a nun's cell.
She loves Lysander. They plan to run tomorrow night
through the wood, to his aunt's, beyond the law.

[Verse 2]
Helena loves Demetrius, but he loves Hermia now.
She tells him of the flight, hoping he'll be kind;
he follows them, she follows him into the trees.
And Quince's craftsmen come to rehearse a wedding play,
Bottom the weaver as Pyramus, Thisbe's love.

[Chorus]
Milk-white once, now purple with the wound,
love-in-idleness under the moon.
Close your eyes, and open soon,
love-in-idleness under the moon.

[Verse 3]
The fairy king and queen are quarreling
over a boy she raises for her dead friend's sake;
their war has drowned the fields and turned the seasons.
Oberon wants the boy. He sends Puck for me:
my juice on sleeping eyes will make you love
the first live creature that you see.
He hears Demetrius scorn Helena: charm that man.

[Verse 4]
Oberon presses me onto his sleeping queen.
Puck finds Athenian clothes, Lysander asleep,
and gives him me. The wrong man.
Helena wakes him; he swears he loves her,
leaves Hermia sleeping on the ground.
Helena thinks it's mockery and runs;
Hermia wakes, and the wood is empty.

[Chorus]
Milk-white once, now purple with the wound,
love-in-idleness under the moon.
Close your eyes, and open soon,
love-in-idleness under the moon.

[Verse 5]
Puck sets a donkey's head on Bottom; his friends flee.
The queen wakes with me in her eyes and loves him,
and her fairies serve him. Oberon sees the mistake
and lays me on Demetrius himself.
Now both men want Helena; she thinks they mock her.
Hermia feels betrayed. The rivals go to duel.

[Bridge]
Puck brings the fog and speaks in their voices,
walks them apart till all four sleep.
Another herb undoes me on Lysander's eyes,
only his.
Demetrius still wears my juice.

[Verse 6]
Oberon says the queen, still charmed, gave up the boy.
His herb undoes me in her eyes; Puck lifts the donkey head
from Bottom's own; the fairies dance in peace.
Theseus' horns wake the four; he overrules Egeus;
three couples will wed, his own among them.
Lysander, cured, loves Hermia again;
Demetrius, still mine, loves Helena,
and says some power changed his heart.
Bottom wakes, can't tell his dream, and finds his friends.

Married, three couples watch the workmen's play:
a Wall, then a Lion stains Thisbe's cloak; Pyramus thinks her dead,
stabs himself; she finds him, does the same. Only acting.
Bottom sits up; the court laughs; two players dance.

[Final Chorus]
Milk-white once, now purple with the wound,
love-in-idleness under the moon.
Close your eyes, and open soon,
love-in-idleness under the moon.

[Outro]
The fairies bless the house.
Puck says, if we offended, call it a dream,
and give us your hands.
Milk-white once, now purple with the wound.

songs.adaptation_note: The master-of-ceremonies voice and the ad libs are interpretive. 'Let him roar again' comes from Bottom's casting boast (I.2.u0040) and is reused here as a chant. remaining_cautions: Bottom's donkey episode is placed in the bridge, after the Lysander mistake, for comic contrast. It is not exact scene-by-scene order.
'Dump' and 'splits' are casual paraphrases of Demetrius's rejection and Helena's exit.

songs.treatment: Moonlit neo soul, about 78 BPM. Puck's country proverb is updated into a slow refrain that the narrator keeps testing against what actually happens.
songs.narrative_lens: An intimate narrator telling the story slowly to a lover ('let me tell it slow, love') in loose, unhurried phrases.
songs.lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Let me tell it slow, love.
Theseus is counting four days
till he marries Hippolyta,
when Egeus walks his daughter in:
Hermia marries Demetrius,
or the law takes her life,
or she lives out her days as a nun.
She loves Lysander, so they whisper a plan:
tomorrow night, through the wood,
to his aunt's, beyond the law.

[Verse 2]
Now Helena loves Demetrius,
and he swore he loved her too,
till he saw Hermia. So she tells him,
hoping for one kind word.
He runs after them; she runs after him.
Same night, Quince's workmen,
Bottom the weaver as Pyramus,
slip out to rehearse a wedding play
where no one's watching.

[Chorus]
Jack gets his Jill, nothing goes ill,
every man gets his own again.
Jack gets his Jill, and all will be well,
but somebody's still under the spell.

[Verse 3]
In that wood a fairy king and queen
are fighting over a boy
she raises for his mother, her friend who died,
and the seasons come undone.
Oberon wants the boy. He sends Puck for a flower:
one drop on sleeping eyes,
you love the first live thing you see.
He hears Demetrius cast Helena off.
Puck, charm that man.

[Verse 4]
He drops it on his sleeping queen.
Puck sees Athenian clothes on Lysander
and takes him for the man.
Helena wakes him; he swears he loves her,
leaves Hermia sleeping in the dark.
Helena thinks he's mocking her, and goes;
Hermia wakes to no one.

[Chorus]
Jack gets his Jill, nothing goes ill,
every man gets his own again.
Jack gets his Jill, and all will be well,
but somebody's still under the spell.

[Verse 5]
Puck gives Bottom a donkey's head; his friends run.
Titania wakes, enchanted, loves him, has her fairies feed him honey.
Oberon catches the mistake and touches Demetrius' eyes himself.
Both men woo Helena; she calls it cruelty.
Hermia feels betrayed; the men go off to duel,
but Puck brings the fog, speaks in each man's voice,
and walks them round till all four lie down.

[Bridge]
Cure on Lysander's eyes, and only his.
Demetrius still wears the flower's kiss.
Oberon says the queen, while charmed, gave up the boy;
he frees her; Puck lifts the donkey head from Bottom's own,
and the fairies dance.

[Verse 6]
Dawn horns: Theseus finds the lovers and overrules Egeus;
three couples will wed, his own among them.
Lysander's back with Hermia;
Demetrius, still enchanted, loves Helena,
says some power turned his heart.
Bottom wakes, can't say his dream,
runs back to his crew.

[Verse 7]
At the feast, the couples watch the play:
lovers whisper through a Wall; a Lion stains Thisbe's cloak;
Pyramus thinks her dead,
stabs himself; she finds him, does the same. Just acting.
The couples laugh, the players dance,
and the fairies bless the house.

[Final Chorus]
Jack gets his Jill, nothing goes ill,
every man gets his own again.
Jack gets his Jill, and all will be well,
but somebody's still under the spell.

[Outro]
Puck says, if we offended, think it was a dream;
pardon us, and give us your hands.
Jack gets his Jill. Nothing goes ill?
